audit.why: Tricky early poke lane, Vladimir tilts it from levels 4-5 on and outscales; TRICKY 7/10 fits a 50.59% WR over 4129 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart had Viktor on row 3 and blanket 'Skill' on rows 4-6 while content win[] and the packet levelChart give Vladimir rows 3-6.
audit.why: Packet levelChart: Viktor x3 then Vladimir x4; content whys already argue Vladimir takes over at 4-5.
audit.corrected: Full sides moved to Vladimir on rows 3-6 with whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Outdated ability names throughout the content layer: 'Death Ray' (now Hextech Ray), 'Chaos Storm' (now Arcane Storm), 'hex cores'/'upgrade' (now Hex Fragments/augments from Glorious Evolution). Packet suspectNames confirmed Death Ray; 'Siphon Power's' in early is a FALSE POSITIVE — correct possessive of the real Q name.
audit.why: enemyKit lists E Hextech Ray, R Arcane Storm, P Glorious Evolution with Hex Fragment augments.
audit.corrected: All occurrences renamed; augment phrasing used.

audit.why: Kit gives W 17-13s, E 12-8s and 60+ mana, Vlad W 28s.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. It governs your forward steps. - W Sanguine Pool spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Gravity Field is 17s at rank 1, 13s max — the stun zone owns every all-in; walk out the moment it drops and commit only on its downtime. - Hextech Ray runs 12s down to 8s and costs 60+ mana — his dry spells are your trade windows. - Your 28s Pool spent on poke is a death you scheduled.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, E-charge as he steps to answer, release and walk — the trade costs him HP and pays yours.
edits.after: Gravity Field's stun is his only setup — Pool it and its 17-second cooldown leaves his all-in with no lock.

edits.before: Pooling his poke and then eating the real engage at half HP with nothing — the pool is a combo-breaker, not a flinch reflex.
edits.after: A full E charge holds you visible for over a second — at half HP in Hextech Ray range that is the burst window he waits for.

edits.before: The crimson rush timing — Q empowers every third-ish cast and the sustain war starts tilting your way.
edits.after: Crimson Rush now empowers every third-ish Q and your sustain out-heals his mana-limited poke — lane tilts to you.

edits.before: Hemoplague online — the all-in inverts: Q-E-R-E with ignite kills most mids who thought they were winning.
edits.after: Hemoplague online before his Hextech Ray augment — Q-E-R with ignite kills a Viktor holding only one Q shield.

edits.before: Riftmaker timing: every trade heals more than it costs. Extended fights are now donations to your health bar.
edits.after: Riftmaker timing: every trade heals more than it costs, and an immobile Viktor cannot stop the walk-down.

edits.before: Late Vlad is a raid boss: pool their engage, R their clump, and drain whatever stayed to argue.
edits.after: Late Vlad is a raid boss: pool his Arcane Storm, R the clump, and drain whatever stayed to argue.

edits.before: At 6 Hemoplague plus Sanguine Pool all-in beats him before his Death Ray upgrade.
edits.after: At 6 Hemoplague plus Sanguine Pool all-in beats him before his Hextech Ray augment.

edits.before: Your Hemoplague plus Sanguine Pool spike lands before his upgraded E Death Ray online, giving you an all-in window; Pool the Gravity Field stun and dive while your sustain out-heals his single Q shield.
edits.after: Your Hemoplague plus Sanguine Pool spike lands before his augmented E Hextech Ray, giving you an all-in window; Pool the Gravity Field stun and dive while your sustain out-heals his single Q shield.

edits.before: Vladimir outscales: your Pool dodges his upgraded Death Ray and Chaos Storm ult, Zhonya's negates his combo, and Hemoplague's amp plus your durability let you dive a squishy immobile Viktor.
edits.after: Vladimir outscales: your Pool dodges his augmented Hextech Ray and Arcane Storm ult, Zhonya's negates his combo, and Hemoplague's amp plus your durability let you dive a squishy immobile Viktor.

edits.before: From Lvl 4 your Transfusion sustain out-heals his poke, and at 6 Sanguine Pool plus Hemoplague gives you an all-in that arrives before his upgraded Death Ray, letting you Pool his Gravity Field and turn the lane your way.
edits.after: From Lvl 4 your Transfusion sustain out-heals his poke, and at 6 Sanguine Pool plus Hemoplague gives you an all-in that arrives before his augmented Hextech Ray, letting you Pool his Gravity Field and turn the lane your way.

edits.before: You outscale an immobile Viktor at 2+ items: Zhonya's and your Pool absorb his Death Ray and Chaos Storm combo, and Hemoplague's teamfight amp plus your drain durability make you the bigger threat than a squishy control mage.
edits.after: You outscale an immobile Viktor at 2+ items: Zhonya's and your Pool absorb his Hextech Ray and Arcane Storm combo, and Hemoplague's teamfight amp plus your drain durability make you the bigger threat than a squishy control mage.

edits.before: Pool the Gravity Field stun and dive before his Death Ray upgrade
edits.after: Pool the Gravity Field stun and dive before his Hextech Ray augment

edits.before: Free-farm hex cores to spike his upgraded Death Ray and Chaos Storm
edits.after: Free-farm Hex Fragments to augment Hextech Ray and Arcane Storm

notes: Viktor was reworked: E is Hextech Ray (not Death Ray), R is Arcane Storm (not Chaos Storm), passive is Glorious Evolution with Hex Fragment augments (not hex cores) — all renamed. Packet suspectName 'Siphon Power's' in early is a false positive (correct possessive). Kit flags Viktor R as 'channel: interruptible' but Riot's own text describes a persistent storm that interrupts ENEMY channels — trusted the description and made no claim that CC cancels his R. Sweep: breakdown.early, breakdown.carry, breakdown.feeding, ahead, enemyWin remain structurally templated; nothing Viktor-specific could be grounded there without inventing, recorded rather than written.
